review_items.rationale: Applicability: The obligation is conditional on no contact with a required remote voter and an already-expired prior marker. The public lease contract supports role loss in that condition. Counting a real negative heartbeat as contact is an alternative outside the no-response antecedent. This interpretation does not require every pipeline error to imply no receiver processing; the harness independently supplies no receiver worker. Decomposition: Real timeout publication -> real pipeline consumer -> contact marker -> actual lease decision addresses the selected A2 relation. The oracle observes role after lease consumption, not merely the response-interface mismatch. Ordinary timeout is an independent comparison. Even if this obligation held, stale reads or incorrect commits could still arise through other mechanisms; it is not sufficient for overall correctness. Checker correspondence: Saved checker selects independent lease_result events, correlates operation with prefix and completed events, and asserts State == Follower. Raw execution has no parse errors, correlated results 3 and 7, pipeline command timed out with same_request=true, actual contact refresh and Leader result, plus ordinary timeout unchanged contact and Follower result. Completion is awaited before result; receiver processing/replies are structurally absent; result is not a prerequisite. However saved harness uses DefaultConfig (HeartbeatTimeout and ElectionTimeout 1s), sets LeaderLeaseTimeout to 2s, then bypasses ValidateConfig by storing config directly. config.go rejects lease greater than heartbeat. This prevents attribution to a supported configuration even though the local measurement is intact. Repair by setting HeartbeatTimeout and ElectionTimeout to at least 2s, calling ValidateConfig before execution, retaining lease 2s, prior contact 4s, oracle, prerequisites and actual transport paths. Fresh execution and focused review must resolve this issue; a source-only assurance is insufficient.
counterevidence: src-default-and-valid-config: DefaultConfig supplies HeartbeatTimeout=1s; ValidateConfig rejects LeaderLeaseTimeout > HeartbeatTimeout and ElectionTimeout < HeartbeatTimeout.
limitations: Conditional local prefix is not established by an election history.
Harness configuration validity is challenged separately below.
Fallback replication, incoming RPCs, heartbeat and VerifyLeader workers are omitted and may alter full-node role duration.
No observed application endpoint or automatic lease scheduling.
Initial Leader state and expired marker remain explicit constructed premises after configuration repair.
State reports local role; this is not a claim of global leadership or a client completion.

selections.rationale: Register the initial partial map and preserve a concrete A2 contact-marker question. Code establishes heterogeneous marker qualification; documentation weakens a naive successful-acknowledgement interpretation. No obligation or Evidence is claimed. Next discriminator is applicability of higher-term response handling and whether independent replication or incoming RPC processing necessarily closes the suspected window.

Continue the same principal contact-marker lifecycle. The heartbeat-rejection variant has no acquired immediate-role-loss requirement; pipeline timeout is a stronger discriminator because it can create a fresh marker without a delivered reply, and the response interface explicitly limits validity to successful completion. Register this newly read dependency before constructing a local executed comparison. Do not infer a lease failure solely from the interface mismatch.

feedback.answered: The contact-only contract does not demand successful heartbeat acceptance. Newly read producer code also shows that pipeline readiness does not imply response success: timeouts publish futures, while the existing consumer reads response fields directly. Ordinary periodic replication is an alternate step-down route, not a proven finite bound under arbitrary delays.
remaining: Requirement gap narrowed: AppendFuture.Response explicitly requires Error completion and success; the lease contract concerns actual contact, but an API mismatch alone is not a completed authority-loss finding.
Local execution gap: run a real in-memory pipeline timeout, correlate its request/future identity, observe Error and marker before/after actual pipelineDecode consumption.
Initial-prefix and same-history gaps: full cluster election, pipeline activation and isolated no-contact interval have not been executed. Remote processing without reply remains possible.

Endpoint gap: whether this refresh changes a scheduled lease decision or public leadership-loss timing remains unobserved; fallback replication and negative verification remain protective alternatives.
